_meta.indication: Bepreve (bepotastine besilate ophthalmic solution) 1.5% is a histamine H1 receptor antagonist indicated for the treatment of itching associated with signs and symptoms of allergic conjunctivitis.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, vehicle-controlled conjunctival allergen challenge (CAC) study
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with allergic conjunctivitis undergoing ocular allergen challenge
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Ocular itching evaluated by the subject at 3, 5, and 7 minutes post challenge (0-4 unit scale)
pivotal_trials.n: N=35 bepotastine 1.5%, N=36 bepotastine 1%, N=36 vehicle
pivotal_trials.result: Bepotastine 1.5% achieved statistically significant reduction in ocular itching vs vehicle; at Visit 5 (Day 28)-CAC at 15 minutes post-dosing, mean itching grade difference (vehicle - active) of 1.4 at 3 min post-CAC, p<0.001

nct_ctgov.title: Evaluation of the Onset and Duration of Action of Bepotastine Besilate Ophthalmic Solution in Acute Allergic Conjunctivitis

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, vehicle-controlled conjunctival allergen challenge (CAC) study
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with allergic conjunctivitis undergoing ocular allergen challenge
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Ocular itching evaluated by the subject at 3, 5, and 7 minutes post challenge (0-4 unit scale)
pivotal_trials.n: N=43 bepotastine 1.5%, N=44 bepotastine 1%, N=43 vehicle
pivotal_trials.result: Bepotastine 1.5% achieved statistically significant reduction in ocular itching vs vehicle; at Visit 5 (Day 28)-CAC at 15 minutes post-dosing, mean itching grade difference (vehicle - active) of 1.5 at 3 min post-CAC, p<0.001

key_safety: Most common adverse reaction was a mild taste following instillation (~25% of subjects); other reactions occurring in 2-5% were eye irritation, headache, and nasopharyngitis.
target_moa: Bepotastine is a topically active, direct H1-receptor antagonist and an inhibitor of the release of histamine from mast cells.

rems.type: No risk management activities were recommended beyond routine monitoring and reporting of adverse events.

advisory_committee.vote: The Dermatologic and Ophthalmic Drugs Advisory Committee met June 26, 2009 and unanimously concluded that adequate safety and efficacy had been demonstrated for the treatment of itching due to allergic conjunctivitis.

summary.text: Standard 505(b)(1) NDA submitted November 12, 2008 and approved as recommended; the Dermatologic and Ophthalmic Drugs Advisory Committee unanimously supported approval, and no postmarketing requirements or Phase 4 commitments were required.
